### Install OpenCode with Bun

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/index.mdx

Install the `opencode-ai` package globally using Bun.

```bash
bun install -g opencode-ai
```

--------------------------------

### Install dependencies and start development CLI/TUI

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md

Installs dependencies and runs the V2 CLI and TUI. Pass a directory path to target another project or . for the current repository.

```bash
bun install
bun dev [directory]
```

--------------------------------

### Run /connect command in the TUI

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/index.mdx

Run this command in the TUI to start connecting a provider, then select opencode and head to opencode.ai/auth.

```txt
/connect
```

--------------------------------

### Define main setup with Plugin.MainSetup in src/gui/main.ts

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Use Plugin.MainSetup for the main setup, which runs on desktop only. This example writes a log message.

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export const main: Plugin.MainSetup = (ctx) => {
  ctx.log.write("info", "acme started")
}
```

### Config discovery example starting from packages/web

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/config.mdx

Example directory tree when starting OpenCode from /home/user/projects/acme/packages/web. OpenCode searches from the current directory to the filesystem root, merging direct configs first, then .opencode configs.

```text
/etc/opencode/opencode.json
~/.config/opencode/opencode.json

/home/user/projects/acme/
├── opencode.json
└── packages/
    └── web/
        ├── opencode.json
        └── src/
```

### Window setup with createKeyed and cleanup function

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Window setup must be synchronous; start asynchronous work inside createKeyed or createLatest. Registrations made through ctx are withdrawn when the component or createKeyed run disposes. Return a cleanup function for other resources such as timers.

```tsx
import { Command, createKeyed, Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { Changes } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/review"

export default Plugin.define({
  i18n: { en: { changes: "Show changes" } },
  setup(ctx) {
    // Runs once per active generation of Changes; the command is withdrawn with it.
    createKeyed(ctx.use(Changes), (changes) => {
      ctx.add(Command, () => ({
        id: "changes",
        title: ctx.t("changes"),
        run: () => {
          const session = ctx.sessions.current()

          if (session) changes.open(session)
        },
      }))
    })

    const timer = setInterval(() => console.log("still here"), 60_000)

    return () => clearInterval(timer)
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Define window setup with Plugin.Setup in src/gui/window.tsx

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Type the window setup from the declared definition using Plugin.Setup<typeof definition>. This types ctx.stores from the declared stores. Import the Notes token from ./contract.

```tsx
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { Notes } from "./contract"
import type { definition } from "./definition"

export const setup: Plugin.Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  ctx.provide(Notes, { count: () => ctx.stores.notes.value.count })
}
```

--------------------------------

### Initial load and background plugin boot flow

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/specs/v2/catalog-config-plugin-lifecycle.md

Illustrates building a baseline catalog from immediate sources while background fibers activate slower plugins asynchronously.

```ts
LocationServiceMap.get(ref)
  → build location layer
    → Catalog.layer creates empty catalog state
    → PluginBoot.layer activates immediately available plugins
      → ConfigProviderPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → ModelsDevPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → AuthPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
    → Catalog.layer applies active transforms during boot
    → apply policy
    → materialize baseline provider/model catalog
  → PluginBoot baseline ready
    → Frontend.fetchCatalog()

PluginBoot background fiber
  → install/update plugin packages concurrently
  → activate completed plugins
    → Catalog.transform()
      → transform(updateCatalog)
        → Catalog internally rebuilds
          → Catalog.Event.Updated
            → Frontend.refetchCatalog()
```

### Combine definition, setup, and main in src/gui.tsx

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Export the plugin by combining the definition, window setup, and main setup with Plugin.define. This is the ./gui-experimental entry point.

```tsx
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { definition } from "./gui/definition"
import { main } from "./gui/main"
import { setup } from "./gui/window"

export default Plugin.define({ ...definition, setup, main })
```

### AGENTS.md load order example

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/instructions.mdx

All four files from the discovery example are loaded and combined in this order. OpenCode combines the files and does not resolve conflicts between them.

```text
~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md
packages/web/AGENTS.md
packages/AGENTS.md
AGENTS.md
```

### Set environment variables for an LSP server with env

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/lsp.mdx

Use the `env` property to set environment variables when starting the LSP server. The example sets `RUST_LOG` to `debug` for rust-analyzer.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "lsp": {
    "rust": {
      "command": ["rust-analyzer"],
      "env": {
        "RUST_LOG": "debug"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Support V1 and V2 from one package with server() and setup()

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/migrate-v1.mdx

A package can temporarily expose both implementations from one default export: V1 calls `server()` and V2 calls `setup()`. The APIs remain separate; this shape does not translate hooks automatically. V1 object entrypoints are supported in OpenCode `1.18.29` and newer.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default {
  ...Plugin.define({
    id: "example",
    async setup(ctx) {
      await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      })
    },
  }),
  async server() {
    return {
      "tool.execute.before": async () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      },
    }
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### Install OpenCode via install script and package managers

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/README.md

Installation commands for OpenCode across multiple package managers. Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

```bash
# YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash

# Package managers
npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest      # or bun/pnpm/yarn
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2 # macOS and Linux (recommended, always up to date)
brew install opencode              # macOS and Linux (official brew formula, updated less)
sudo pacman -S opencode            # Arch Linux (Stable)
paru -S opencode-beta              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
mise use -g opencode               # Any OS
nix run github:anomalyco/opencode  # Nix
```

### Return a cleanup function from setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

setup runs when the plugin loads and may return a cleanup function that runs when the plugin unloads. Use ctx.app.version to read the OpenCode version.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  setup(ctx) {
    console.log(`loaded in OpenCode ${ctx.app.version}`)
    return () => console.log("unloaded")
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Export V1 server() and V2 setup() from one plugin entrypoint

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

Default-export an object combining a V1 `server()` function with a V2 `setup()` function so one package entrypoint supports both versions. V1 calls `server()` and uses its returned hooks; V2 reads `id` and `setup()` and ignores `server()`. Spread `Plugin.define(...)` into the exported object so the V2 definition type-checks separately from `server()`.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default {
  ...Plugin.define({
    id: "example",
    async setup(ctx) {
      await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      })
    },
  }),
  async server() {
    return {
      "tool.execute.before": async () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      },
    }
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

Installs the plugin directly from the Git repository's Figma directory using the default branch.

opencode plugin add 'git+https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode.git#path:packages/plugins/figma'
```

--------------------------------

### V2 plugin entrypoint with Plugin.define and setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/migrate-v1.mdx

V2 plugins default-export a definition with an `id` and `setup(ctx)`. Every V2 plugin needs a stable `id`; plugin storage is scoped by this ID, and the ID also identifies the plugin in status and diagnostics.

```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await ctx.storage.set("last-project", ctx.location.project.id)
    console.log(`Loaded for ${ctx.location.directory}`)
  },
})
```

### Install OpenCode on Arch Linux

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/index.mdx

The official Arch package installs OpenCode 2; use the AUR `opencode-bin` package to install OpenCode 1.

```bash
sudo pacman -S opencode           # Arch Linux (OpenCode 2)
paru -S opencode-bin              # Arch Linux (OpenCode 1, from AUR)
```

### Description

```
```

### Define a GUI plugin setup with SettingsPage and Command

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-plugins/README.md

Use this setup function to register a settings page and command for a GUI plugin. It lazily loads the page, preloads it on idle, and conditionally adds remote access and keep-screen-active entries only when pairing is active.

```tsx
import { lazy, onCleanup, Suspense } from "solid-js"
import { Command, SettingsPage, type Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { onIdle } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/builtin"
import { Pairing } from "./contract"
import type definition from "./index"

const setup: Plugin.Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.desktop) return
  const layout = ctx.layout
  const servers = ctx.servers
  const pairing = ctx.use(Pairing)
  const Page = lazy(() => import("./page"))
  // Settings rows are small; load them while idle so settings opens without a blank row.
  onCleanup(onIdle(() => void Page.preload()))

  // The desktop's own server. Its ref is already authenticated in this window, so codes need no main process.
  const local = () =>
    servers
      .list()
      .map((id) => servers.get(id))
      .find((server) => server?.builtin)

  ctx.add(SettingsPage, {
    id: "pairing",
    icon: "server",
    get title() {
      return ctx.t("title")
    },
    get entries() {
      const pairingEntry = { id: "pairing", title: ctx.t("title"), keywords: "pair device qr phone remote" }

      // Remote access and the display setting exist only while pairing's main side answers.
      if (pairing().status !== "active") return [pairingEntry]

      return [
        pairingEntry,
        {
          id: "settings-remote-access",
          title: ctx.t("remote.title"),
          description: ctx.t("remote.description"),
          keywords: "internet tunnel opentunnel",
        },
        {
          id: "settings-keep-screen-active",
          title: ctx.t("screenActive.title"),
          description: ctx.t("screenActive.description"),
          keywords: "display sleep awake local",
        },
      ]
    },
    render: () => (
      <Suspense>
        <Page server={local} pairing={pairing} />
      </Suspense>
    ),
  })

  ctx.add(Command, () => ({
    id: "open",
    title: ctx.t("command.title"),
    group: ctx.t("command.category.server"),
    run: () => layout.settings("pairing"),
  }))
}

export default setup
```

--------------------------------

### Define GUI plugin with setup and main in src/gui.tsx

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Each process evaluates the whole ./gui-experimental file and reads its default export. Windows run setup, and the desktop app's main process runs main. Keep each process's code inside its own setup because the other process's modules are inert placeholders.

```tsx
import { shell } from "electron"
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export default Plugin.define({
  setup(ctx) {
    // Window code: Solid components, ctx.layout, ctx.add(Command, …).
  },
  main(ctx) {
    // Main code: electron, Node built-ins, ctx.windows.
    ctx.windows.on("open", () => shell.beep())
  },
})
```

Add custom LSP servers by specifying the command and file extensions. The example defines a server named `custom-lsp`.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "lsp": {
    "custom-lsp": {
      "command": ["custom-lsp-server", "--stdio"],
      "extensions": [".custom"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Register a Server with ready, entries, and http

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Use to contribute a list of server connections, such as servers your plugin starts on other machines. Startup waits for every source to be ready; a ready source's entries are its complete inventory. Each entry's key is <plugin id>:<id>.

```ts
import { Server } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

ctx.add(
  Server,
  (): Server => ({
    ready: loaded(),
    entries: machines().map((machine) => ({
      id: machine.id,
      name: machine.name,
      label: "Acme",
      state: machine.url ? "ready" : "starting",
      http: machine.url ? { url: machine.url } : undefined,
    })),
  }),
)
```

### Access TUI plugin context values in setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

The setup function receives configuration, app metadata, the current location, the OpenCode client, cached data, theme tokens, the OpenTUI renderer, and UI APIs. Use context.options, context.location, context.app, context.client, context.renderer, and context.theme to access them.

```ts
setup(context) {
  const compact = context.options.compact === true
  const location = context.location ?? context.data.location.default()
  const version = context.app.version
  const channel = context.app.channel
  const client = context.client
  const renderer = context.renderer
  const theme = context.theme
}
```

### TextNode Range Methods

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-figjam/references/edit-text.md

SDK methods on TextNode for getting and setting properties across a specific character range (start to end indices).

```APIDOC
## TextNode Range Methods

### Description
Methods available on `TextNode` instances to apply mixed styling, fonts, fills, hyperlinks, and list options to specific character ranges.

### Methods
- `textNode.setRangeFontName(start, end, fontName)`
- `textNode.setRangeFontSize(start, end, size)`
- `textNode.setRangeFills(start, end, fills)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextDecoration(start, end, decoration)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextCase(start, end, textCase)`
- `textNode.setRangeLetterSpacing(start, end, spacing)`
- `textNode.setRangeLineHeight(start, end, lineHeight)`
- `textNode.setRangeHyperlink(start, end, hyperlink)`
- `textNode.setRangeListOptions(start, end, listOptions)`
- `textNode.setRangeIndentation(start, end, indentation)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontName(start, end)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontSize(start, end)`

### Usage Examples
```javascript
// Make "Hello" bold (characters 0-5)
textNode.setRangeFontName(0, 5, { family: 'Inter', style: 'Bold' });

// Make "World" red (characters 6-11)
textNode.setRangeFills(6, 11, [{ type: 'SOLID', color: { r: 1, g: 0, b: 0 } }]);

// Change size of "World"
textNode.setRangeFontSize(6, 11, 24);

// Get properties for a range
const fontAtStart = textNode.getRangeFontName(0, 1);
const sizeAtEnd = textNode.getRangeFontSize(10, 11);
```
```

--------------------------------

### Define project instructions in AGENTS.md

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/ar/rules.mdx

An example AGENTS.md file configuring project structure, code standards, and monorepo conventions for an SST v3 project.

```markdown
# SST v3 Monorepo Project

This is an SST v3 monorepo with TypeScript. The project uses bun workspaces for package management.

## Project Structure

- `packages/` - Contains all workspace packages (functions, core, web, etc.)
- `infra/` - Infrastructure definitions split by service (storage.ts, api.ts, web.ts)
- `sst.config.ts` - Main SST configuration with dynamic imports

## Code Standards

- Use TypeScript with strict mode enabled
- Shared code goes in `packages/core/` with proper exports configuration
- Functions go in `packages/functions/`
- Infrastructure should be split into logical files in `infra/`

## Monorepo Conventions

- Import shared modules using workspace names: `@my-app/core/example`
```

### Define a Contract with Contract.define in contract.ts

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Use `Contract.define` when one plugin's window setup exposes an API or a Solid component to other plugins' window setups. The token ID must start with the plugin's own ID.

```ts
import type { JSX } from "solid-js"
import { Contract } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export interface AcmeBadge {
  Badge(props: { readonly label: string }): JSX.Element
  count(): number
}

export const AcmeBadge = Contract.define<AcmeBadge, "acme.badge">("acme.badge")
```

### SetupContext and Context interface reference

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

TypeScript interface definitions for SetupContext and Context, listing the properties and methods available on the plugin context. SetupContext extends Context with a stores record; Context includes options, client, app, signal, add, list, provide, use, main, t, plural, and various host API properties.

```ts
interface SetupContext<D> extends Context {
  stores: Record<string, Persisted<unknown> | ((session: SessionRef) => Persisted<unknown>)>
}

interface Context {
  id: string
  options: PluginOptions
  client: OpenCodeClient
  app: App
  signal: AbortSignal
  add<T>(registry: Registry<T>, item: () => T | undefined): Cleanup
  add<T>(registry: Registry<T>, item: T): Cleanup
  list<T>(registry: Registry<T>): T[]
  provide<T>(token: Contract<T>, impl: T): Cleanup
  use<T>(token: Contract<T>): () => Live<T>
  use<S extends IpcSpec>(token: Ipc<S>): () => Live<IpcClient<S>>
  main<S extends IpcSpec>(token: Ipc<S>): IpcClient<S>
  t(key: string, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): string
  plural(key: string, count: number, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): string
  layout: Layout
  sessions: Sessions
  screen: Screen
  servers: Servers
  storage: Storage
  dialogs: Dialogs
  toast: Toasts
  attention: Attention
  tabs: Tabs
  keybinds: Keybinds
  commands: Commands
  links: Links
  embeds: Embeds
  ui: Ui
  system: System
  desktop: Desktop | undefined
  locale: Locale
  appearance: Appearance
  router: Router
  workspaces: Workspaces
}
```

### Async main setup with ctx.onCleanup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

main may be async. Return, or resolve to, a cleanup function for resources it opens, or register it with ctx.onCleanup(fn). ctx.onCleanup runs its functions when the plugin is disabled, reloaded, or removed, or the app quits, last registered first.

```ts
async main(ctx) {
  const socket = await connect(ctx.options)

  ctx.onCleanup(() => socket.close())
}
```

### Configure Atomic Chat local provider in opencode.json

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx

Defines a custom provider ID `atomic-chat` using `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` pointed at the local Atomic Chat server at `http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1`. Each model ID must match an id returned by `GET /v1/models`; change the host and port to match your setup.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "atomic-chat": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Atomic Chat (local)",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "<your-model-id>": {
          "name": "<your-model-name>"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Set and get CORS origin for OpenCode service

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/troubleshooting.mdx

Use when a browser client on another origin cannot connect because of CORS. Use an exact HTTP or HTTPS origin, including the port when needed, without a path or trailing slash. Setting service configuration stops the background service; its next start picks up the new configuration.

```bash
opencode service set cors http://192.168.1.10:3001
opencode service get cors
```

### Handle Live<T> states with ctx.use(Browser) in a command

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Use ctx.use(token) to get an accessor for a reactive Live<T> that reflects the provider's state. The plugin keeps running while the provider is off, so handle non-active states to avoid dead controls or endless spinners. The example enables a command only when the provider is active and a session exists.

```ts
import { Browser } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/browser"

const browser = ctx.use(Browser)

ctx.add(Command, () => {
  const live = browser()
  const session = ctx.sessions.current()

  return {
    id: "preview",
    title: ctx.t("command.preview"),
    enabled: live.status === "active" && !!session,
    run: () => {
      if (live.status === "active" && session) live.value.open(session, "http://localhost:3000")
    },
  }
})
```

### Automatically review pull requests with OpenCode

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/github.mdx

Use this workflow to automatically review PRs when they are opened or updated. If no `prompt` is provided, OpenCode defaults to reviewing the pull request. `issues: write` lets OpenCode react to and comment on the PR, since GitHub handles PR comments through the issues API. This example is intended for PRs from branches in the same repository; PRs from forks normally get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and no secrets.

```yaml
name: opencode-review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: anomalyco/opencode/github@latest
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
          use_github_token: true
          prompt: |
            Review this pull request:
            - Check for code quality issues
            - Look for potential bugs
            - Suggest improvements
```

### ctx.layout.settings(page?)

--------------------------------

### Define a plugin with Plugin.define and async setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/README.md

Use Plugin.define to register a plugin with an id and async setup. Setup registers hooks imperatively via each domain's hook method, such as ctx.provider.transform.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  setup: async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.provider.transform((editor) => {
      editor.update("example", (provider) => {
        provider.name = "Example"
      })
    })
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Sync, list, get, and invalidate shells by location

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

Shell data operations are scoped to a location. Pass the location to sync, list, get, and invalidate. Call sync before list or get to refresh the data.

```typescript
await context.data.shell.sync(context.location)
const shells = context.data.shell.list(context.location)
const shell = context.data.shell.get(shellID)
context.data.shell.invalidate(context.location)
```

--------------------------------

### Run performance benchmarks with strobe bench

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/app/perf/README.md

Use these commands to compare dev with a worktree, check cases, filter, set parameters, verify method soundness, test desktop channels, and run core/UI benchmarks. The snapshot fixtures must be generated once before running the snapshot benchmark.

```sh
# Did my change help? Compare dev with this worktree.
strobe bench packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts --base origin/dev --head .

# Does the file still work after a change to the app? Each case once, pass or fail with a screenshot.
strobe bench packages/app/perf/tabs.bench.ts --check

# One case, one parameter value, or the whole sweep (Home and review run two sizes unless asked).
strobe bench packages/app/perf/tabs.bench.ts --base origin/dev --head . --filter "open an unvisited*"
strobe bench packages/app/perf/home.bench.ts --base origin/dev --head . --params sessions=5000
strobe bench packages/app/perf/review.bench.ts --base origin/dev --head . --params all

# Is the method sound on this machine? The same build on both sides must come out "same".
strobe bench packages/app/perf/timeline.bench.ts --aa --head .

# Two installed desktop channels, or the desktop's launch (packages/desktop/README.md).
strobe bench packages/app/perf/desktop.bench.ts --base app:opencode --head app:opencode-beta
strobe bench packages/desktop/perf/startup.bench.ts --target desktop --base app:opencode --head app:opencode-beta

# Core and UI code, in a Bun process. The snapshot fixtures are generated once (a minute or two).
bun packages/core/perf/snapshot.ts medium opencode
strobe bench packages/core/perf/snapshot.bench.ts --base origin/dev --head .

# The interactive report, and the tables and rerun command for a pull request body.
strobe report experiment <exp_…> --open
strobe report experiment <exp_…> --format pr
```

### Define complete Q1 launch roadmap Gantt diagram

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/gantt.md

Demonstrates a realistic product-launch roadmap with phases, state tags, task dependencies, and milestone tracking.

```mermaid
gantt
    title Q1 Launch Plan
    dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    section Discovery
    User research   :done, r1, 2026-01-05, 2w
    Synthesis       :done, s1, after r1, 1w
    section Design
    Concepts        :active, d1, after s1, 2w
    Design review   :d2, after d1, 3d
    Hi-fi designs   :d3, after d2, 2w
    section Build
    API scaffolding :b1, after d2, 2w
    UI build        :b2, after d3, 3w
    Integration     :b3, after b2, 1w
    section Launch
    Internal beta   :l1, after b3, 1w
    Fixes           :crit, l2, after l1, 5d
    Ship            :milestone, after l2, 0d
```
